about: Turning hardware identifiers into fingerprints, and deciding whether what a machine reports describes the machine a license names. The threshold is measured against what was collected, not against what was stamped.

cases.name: hash ["4c4c4544-0032"]
cases.why: one identifier hashes to one fingerprint

cases.name: hash ["  4C4C4544-0032  "]
cases.why: case and surrounding whitespace do not make a different machine

cases.name: hash ["4C4C4544-0032", "4c4c4544-0032"]
cases.why: the same identifier read through two interfaces counts once, so it cannot inflate the match threshold

cases.name: hash ["To be filled by O.E.M.", "abc"]
cases.why: a firmware placeholder identifies nothing and is dropped rather than hashed

cases.name: hash ["00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"]
cases.why: an all-zero UUID is a placeholder too

cases.name: hash ["", "   ", "none"]
cases.why: reading nothing usable produces nothing, never a constant

cases.name: the digest itself
cases.why: every binding hashes the same bytes the same way, or none of the matching cases mean anything

cases.name: match ["c"] against ["a", "b", "c"]
cases.why: a container redeployed without its DMI mount reads one of three and keeps working

cases.name: match ["x", "b", "c"] against ["a", "b", "c"]
cases.why: a replaced mainboard changes one identifier and keeps working

cases.name: match ["c", "y", "z"] against ["a", "b", "c"]
cases.why: a host that copied one identifier is refused: one of three is below half

cases.name: match ["a", "z"] against ["a", "b"]
cases.why: half of two is one, so one match of two passes

cases.name: match ["y", "z"] against ["a", "b"]
cases.why: nothing in common is a mismatch however few were read

cases.name: match ["a", "b", "y", "z"] against ["a", "b", "c"]
cases.why: four read, two matched: exactly half passes

cases.name: match ["a", "x", "y", "z"] against ["a", "b", "c"]
cases.why: four read, one matched: below half

cases.name: match [] against ["a"]
cases.why: reading nothing is its own answer, held apart from a mismatch so the operator is told to mount the identifiers rather than to reactivate

cases.name: match ["a"] against []
cases.why: a license naming no machine matches no machine
